body.p: These remarks are responsive to the Office action dated August 16, 2024. Prior to entry of this response, claims 1-20 were pending in the application. By way of this response, claims 1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 16, 17, and 20 are amended, and claims 5, 12, 15, and 19 are cancelled without prejudice. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application and allowance of the pending claims.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to an abstract idea, a mental process of evaluation without significantly more.
Claim 1 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to non-statutory subject matter.
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection but has amended claim 1 to further highlight the patent-eligible subject matter. Amended claim 1 recites:

a non-transitory memory component storing software components
and comprising:

component; and
a second memory space storing a second software component and a stub software component, the first software component configured to interact with the second software component via the proxy
software component and the stub software component; and
at least one processor for executing software components stored on

the first and second memory spaces such that the first software component is configured to perform a polling event of a sensor component stored in the first memory space to obtain a speed reading of the vehicle, perform a comparison event to compare the speed reading to a target speed, generate a command for engine output torque based on the comparison, and send the command to the proxy software component as a command event, and the proxy software component is configured to send the command event to the
stub software component,
wherein the activity monitor software component is arranged when
executed to:
monitor the polling event, the comparison event, and the command event;

events; and

Support for the amendments to claim 1 may be found at least at original claim 5 and paragraphs [0049] and [0051]-[0058] of Applicant's specification.

On page 4 of the Office action, the Office states that claim 1 is directed to transitory signals and thus is not included in the four patent eligible subject matter categories. Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 recites, in part, "a non-transitory memory component storing software components and comprising: a first memory space storing a first software component, a proxy software component, and an activity monitor software component; and a second memory space storing a second software component and a stub software component, the first software component configured to interact with the second software component via the proxy software component and the stub software component." In this way, amended claim 1 includes non-transitory memory and is not directed to transitory signals.

Further, pages 3-4 of the Office action state that the claims are directed to an abstract idea that is not integrated into a practical application, "because the claims fail to identify what is monitored about the vehicle cruise control system and what aspect of the drivetrain is monitored. Therefore, the error message does not have context as to what aspect of the vehicle system is not performing properly." Furthermore, page 4 of the Office action states that the claims do not include additional elements that are sufficient to amount to significantly more than the alleged abstract idea "because the claims fail to identify what aspects of the cruise control are monitored and how the drivetrains performance is correlated to the operation of the cruise control. Therefore, it isn't clear what data is input into the monitoring system, what threshold it is measured against, and then how an error message is conveyed and to whom. The operations are devoid of showing how the claimed invention is use[d]."
Applicant respectfully submits that to the extent that claim 1 includes an abstract idea, the alleged abstract idea is incorporated into a practical application and claim 1

includes significantly more than the alleged abstract idea. Specifically, amended claim 1 recites "at least one processor for executing software components stored on the first and second memory spaces such that the first software component is configured to perform a polling event of a sensor component stored in the first memory space to obtain a speed reading of the vehicle, perform a comparison event to compare the speed reading to a target speed, generate a command for engine output torque based on the comparison, and send the command to the proxy software component as a command event, and the proxy software component is configured to send the command event to the stub software component," and "the activity monitor software component is arranged when executed to: monitor the polling event, the comparison event, and the command event; assess compliance of the polling, comparison, and command events with a schedule of events, wherein assessing compliance includes checking an order and/or a timing of the polling, comparison, and command events; and generate an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events, the error message configured to be displayed, detectable by a diagnostic tool, or used to troubleshoot an error."

Thus, the claims identify what is monitored (e.g., the polling, comparison, and command events, which include polling to obtain a speed reading of the vehicle, comparison of the speed reading to a target speed, and a command for engine output torque based on the comparison) and how the drivetrain performance is correlated to the operation of the cruise control (e.g., compliance of the polling, comparison, and command events, including an order and/or timing of the polling, comparison, and command events, is assessed to generate an error message if non-compliance is detected, and the error message can be used to diagnose or troubleshoot the reason for the non-compliance).

In the rejection, the Office specifically mentions that claim 1 is similar to Example 40 of the 2019 Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance. Example 40 provides two sample claims, one that is determined to be patent eligible (Claim 1) and one that is determined to be ineligible (Claim 2). Applicant submits that amended claim 1 is similar to Claim 1 of Example 40 and thus is patent eligible. Claim 1 of Example 40 was found to be patent eligible due to the claim as a whole being directed to a particular improvement in collecting traffic data, specifically collection of Netflow protocol data when initially collected data reflects an abnormal condition, and the collected data can then be used to analyze the cause

of the abnormal condition. Comparing Claim 1 of Example 40 to Claim 2 of Example 40, Claim 1 includes an element ("collecting additional traffic data relating to the network traffic when the collected traffic data is greater than the predefined threshold, the additional traffic data comprising Netflow protocol data") not included in Claim 2; the claims are otherwise identical. Accordingly, the mere step of collecting Netflow protocol data when the collected traffic data is greater than the predefined threshold is sufficient to incorporate the abstract idea into a practical application.

In the present case, amended claim 1 as a whole is directed to a particular improvement in ensuring system integrity for safety-critical systems (e.g., vehicle cruise control systems) with separated software components. Specifically, the configuration of claim 1 includes an activity monitor that monitors compliance of specific events (e.g., polling, comparison, and command events) to a schedule of events and generates an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events, the error message configured to be displayed, detectable by a diagnostic tool, or used to troubleshoot an error, which allows for any error which could be responsible for erroneous timing and/or order to be investigated and addressed, while maintaining the first software component and the second software component on separate memory spaces. This provides a specific improvement over prior systems, resulting in improved error detection and system robustness against faults. Similar to Example 40, the generated error message can be used to analyze the cause of the non-compliance.
Thus, claim 1 is not directed to a judicial exception or to transitory signals. Accordingly, the rejections should be withdrawn.
Claims 1-9 and 11-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2002/0194551 (Mueller et al., hereinafter Mueller).
Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Mueller in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0343817 (Moellmann).

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections. The cited reference Mueller fails to disclose each and every element of amended claim 1. Mueller is directed to a method and device for monitoring data and data transmission between two control units. The control units have a first program level that calculates control functions and a second program level that monitors the functional reliability of the first level. The first control unit is connected to a component that acquires data, which is then transmitted to the second control unit over a single connection in a secure manner. The data and data transmission are secured separately in the first and second program levels, allowing errors in the data or transmission to be detected.

Whether or not Mueller discloses a watchdog to detect errors in the first program level, Mueller fails to disclose "the activity monitor software component is arranged when executed to: monitor the polling event, the comparison event, and the command event; assess compliance of the polling, comparison, and command events with a schedule of events, wherein assessing compliance includes checking an order and/or a timing of the polling, comparison, and command events; and generate an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events, the error message configured to be displayed, detectable by a diagnostic tool, or used to troubleshoot an error," as claimed in amended claim 1. Rather, Mueller discloses that a message may be checked to see if the message is up-to-date and that the security information of the message may be checked. Applicant believes that this application is now in condition for allowance, in view of the above amendments and remarks. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner issue a Notice of Allowability covering the pending claims.
